Dilution Refrigerator.name: Aluminum
Dilution Refrigerator.reasoning: Used extensively in the construction of the refrigerator's structural parts and thermal shields due to its high thermal conductivity and light weight; very standard material but some components may use copper or stainless steel as alternatives.

Dilution Refrigerator.name: Copper
Dilution Refrigerator.reasoning: Critical for thermal conduction pathways and wiring inside the dilution refrigerator because of its excellent electrical and thermal conductivity; universally used with few or no practical substitutes.

Dilution Refrigerator.name: Stainless steel
Dilution Refrigerator.reasoning: Used for vacuum vessels and mechanical support structures due to its strength and low thermal conductivity reducing heat leak; standard in dilution refrigerator builds though titanium or aluminum alternatives exist.

Dilution Refrigerator.name: Helium
Dilution Refrigerator.reasoning: Primary working fluid (3He/4He isotopes) enabling ultra-low temperature cooling, absolutely essential with no substitutes for dilution refrigeration.

Dilution Refrigerator.name: Silicon
Dilution Refrigerator.reasoning: Used in thermometers, sensors, and some electrical components inside dilution refrigerators; not universal but common and critical for instrumentation.

Dilution Refrigerator.name: Epoxy resins
Dilution Refrigerator.reasoning: Used as adhesives and insulating materials within the refrigerator; commonly used but can be substituted with other polymeric adhesives.

Magnetic Shielding Enclosure.name: Copper
Magnetic Shielding Enclosure.reasoning: Used for electromagnetic shielding layers due to its high conductivity and ability to attenuate magnetic interference; substitution possible with aluminum or other conductive metals but copper is commonly preferred.

Magnetic Shielding Enclosure.name: Aluminum
Magnetic Shielding Enclosure.reasoning: Used for enclosure structure and as a shielding material because of its light weight and good electrical conductivity; commonly used but sometimes replaced by copper or specialized alloys.

Magnetic Shielding Enclosure.name: Steel Ingots
Magnetic Shielding Enclosure.reasoning: Used for structural supports and shells due to mechanical strength; type of steel varies but steel ingots is closest proxy; less critical but very common material in enclosures.
